title: Runtime: memory-pressure + KV-cache guardrails for proactive load shedding (avoid OOM/latency spiral)
creator: Noah Patel
body:
Context
- Under bursty traffic (esp. long prompts + streaming), we’ve seen a failure mode where KV-cache and GPU memory pressure causes:
  1) allocator fragmentation / KV-cache thrash
  2) decode stalls + tail-latency collapse
  3) eventual OOM / engine restart
  4) retry storms + cascading overload
- This ticket adds runtime-level guardrails that shed *before* we hit OOM and before we enter the latency spiral, with deterministic reasons that can be propagated to routing/gateway.

Goals
- Provide a fast, deterministic signal to shed requests when memory pressure is unsafe.
- Preserve control-plane responsiveness by preventing runtime crashes/restarts.
- Emit bounded-cardinality telemetry that can drive breaker inputs and dashboards.
- Ensure streaming correctness: prefer shedding before token emission; avoid partial responses when possible.

Non-goals
- Redesigning scheduler/allocator.
- Solving all memory fragmentation issues (this is a safety rail, not a full optimization).

Proposed behavior (runtime)
Shed triggers (any may trip):
1) KV-cache utilization above hard threshold
   - kv_cache_util = used_blocks / total_blocks
   - Open threshold: 0.90 (configurable per model class)
   - Close threshold: 0.82 (hysteresis)
2) GPU memory free below hard threshold
   - free_bytes < min_free_bytes (configurable; default derived from model + max_seq)
3) Allocation failure / near-OOM signal
   - if allocator returns OOM or repeated retry allocations exceed N attempts in a short window
4) Decode starvation indicator (optional, gated)
   - if decode scheduling lag crosses threshold *and* KV-cache util is high (avoid false positives)

Shed points
- Primary: admission into runtime queue / before prefill scheduling (preferred)
- Secondary: at prefill boundary if pressure rises after queueing (bounded by ENG-4826)
- Avoid shedding mid-decode for streaming requests unless we’re in “hard safety” mode (OOM imminent); in that case return a deterministic abort reason and ensure metrics count it as shed.

Shed reason codes (runtime -> routing)
- RUNTIME_MEMORY_PRESSURE (generic)
- RUNTIME_KV_CACHE_PRESSURE
- RUNTIME_GPU_OOM_RISK

Acceptance criteria
- Runtime returns a deterministic shed response upstream when thresholds are breached (no crash/restart required to recover).
- Guardrails include hysteresis/cooldown to avoid oscillation:
  - once tripped, hold “pressure-open” for at least 10s (configurable) before allowing new admissions.
- Metrics:
  - counter: runtime_shed_total{reason, model, region, pool}
  - gauge: runtime_kv_cache_util{model, pool}
  - gauge: runtime_gpu_mem_free_bytes{pool}
  - counter: runtime_allocator_oom_total{pool}
  - (optional) histogram: runtime_sched_lag_ms{stage=prefill|decode}
- Integration:
  - shed reason is plumbed through routing/gateway error mapping (ENG-4823/ENG-4824 path), including Retry-After guidance from gateway.
- Tests:
  - unit tests for thresholding + hysteresis
  - load test / perf characterization demonstrating:
    - reduced OOMs under synthetic overload
    - improved p99 stability vs baseline (or at least no worse under non-overload)

Implementation notes
- Added a MemoryPressureGuard component in runtime:
  - reads KV-cache block allocator stats per engine
  - reads GPU memory watermark from CUDA allocator API
  - exposes a lightweight “should_admit()” check called at queue admission and before prefill scheduling
- Default thresholds are conservative and intended to be tuned by SRE (ENG-4828) per model class.
- Cardinatlity constraints: model label uses Redwood model slug; pool label uses pool_id (bounded). No tenant/customer labels.

Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag: runtime.memory_pressure_guardrails.enabled
- Canary in us-east on 1–2 hosted models with known long-prompt usage.
- Watch:
  - OOM/restart rate
  - shed rate by reason
  - p99 latency + streaming disconnects

Links
- Related: ENG-4826 (bounded queues + deterministic shed points)
- Related: ENG-4829 (metrics + traces for admission/shed)
- PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18488.json (Runtime memory-pressure guardrail to shed before KV-cache thrash/OOM)
- PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18494.json (Plumb overload reason codes end-to-end)

Updates / comments
- 2025-11-22 (Noah Patel): Seen 2 incidents in last month where KV-cache hit ~95% util and decode latency went nonlinear before OOM. Guardrail should trip earlier and shed at admission.
- 2025-12-03 (Omar El-Sayed): Suggest splitting KV-cache pressure vs generic memory pressure so routing can make better fallback decisions (e.g., same model different pool/region).
- 2025-12-08 (Lena Fischer): Ensure this is checked *before* enqueue to avoid inflating queue and wasting CPU work. Secondary shed at prefill boundary is fine but must be bounded.
- 2025-12-14 (Samir Qureshi): Implemented hysteresis + 10s hold-open to avoid flapping when KV-cache oscillates around threshold.
- 2026-01-07 (Christine Wong): Confirmed reason codes align with breaker taxonomy; ensure we don’t map these to generic 500. Routing should treat as overload-protected.
- 2026-01-20 (Samir Qureshi): Canary results: OOMs reduced to zero in us-east canary during step-function overload test; shed rate increased as expected; p99 stable vs baseline. Shipping broadly behind flag.

Follow-ups
- Consider exposing “recommended max concurrency” hint to routing based on current KV-cache headroom (future work; not required for this ticket).
- Evaluate whether mid-stream hard-shed behavior needs additional client messaging (likely handled in gateway docs + SDK guidance).
